limitations: Corrected material/thermal topology for the current modeled material package; no physical qualification or measured thermal history is established.
Exact commercial motor exterior temperatures are still explicit exploratory bounds, not measured histories.
Closed long-cylinder exchange in each axial band ignores end view factors; not a 3D radiation solution or a universally conservative bound.
Split clamps, pivot holes, sparse rails, drive lugs and non-coaxial servo envelopes need angular visibility and moving-geometry checks.
No path radiates through the opaque motor liner, direct liner/shield contact, or intervening modeled annular shield; real openings and nozzle end exposure remain unmodeled.
The foil shield is an ideal continuous annulus; seam, wrinkles, oxidation, contamination, edge bypass and finite-end view factors are not resolved.
Only the mica liner resolves radial gradients; the radiant foil and other parts are uniform capacities, not surface hot-spot predictions.
Static air conduction, no circulation; external shell convection and upper bay cooling are estimated boundary paths.
Contact conductance ranges are estimates; real fasteners, bonds, printed orientation and temperature-dependent properties require calibration.
Direct mica/foil contact uses series radial half-wall resistance and bounded interface conductance, with no gap-air conduction or radiation at the touching surfaces.
Axial retention/support contacts are lumped part-to-node conductances; liner-side contacts map to its outer radial cell and do not resolve end-face heat spreading or plate hotspots.

Mica thrust-pad cross-section is inferred from recorded CAD volume divided by thickness. Each modeled pad connection adds half-thickness radial conduction in series with an estimated interface conductance; sector contact shape, preload and end-face heat spreading remain unresolved.

The TVC cassette radial surfaces use the CAD grip-ring radii (motor-clear radius to grip outer radius), not its larger forestop/end-block envelope. If any other coincident annular intervals still overlap radially, the later outer annulus is omitted from that band and the excluded pair is recorded; configured lumped support contacts remain active.
Radially averaged nodes do not qualify local hot contact plates, pad edges, fastener holes, or bonded interfaces.
Regular radiative surroundings use emissivity 0.9; the foil outer surface uses 0.1 nominal and 0.3 upper/aged bounds.
Prescribed case boundary has no finite motor heat capacity or plume model; energy residual checks the network, not the motor's available heat.
Neither computed passing temperatures nor convergence authorizes materials, physical work or a flight.
thermal.acceptance_interpretation: required robustness case; a numerical screen pass does not close the absent exact motor history or foil-aging correlation

structural_acceptance: unavailable; changed mount bores require analysis
limitations: All added foil, mica spacers and enlarged mount bores are explicit normal-generator CAD solids with rebuilt mass.
Adjacent foils have serial mica end spacers; no overlapping full-radius spacer disks or invisible ideal gaps are used.
This is a fixed-motor neutral-geometry study; sampled or continuous TVC clearance is not inferred.
Nominal nonintersection does not verify foil roundness, seam, installation, vibration, thermal expansion or tolerances.
Enlarged ring bores require new structural and buckling checks before adoption.
The coaxial model retains finite-end/opening and gas-circulation limitations; passing calculated part means do not qualify hot spots.
Every added foil uses the same configured contaminated emissivity in the required combined case.
Missing exact motor histories and manufactured material/contact measurements remain later verification dependencies.
